title: The Ethical Movement: Its Principles and Aims
author: felix-adler
attributionNote: Associated with Felix Adler, founder of Ethical Culture. The exact bibliographic form and edition require verification before any text is imported.
description: A statement of the Ethical Culture movement’s humanist commitments: the worth of persons, ethical relationships, social reform and the pursuit of the good life without supernatural doctrine.
historicalContext: Ethical Culture emerged in late nineteenth-century New York and spread through affiliated societies. It is a small movement with varied local expressions and should not be treated as a single global church.
